source.prompt: Which CRMs have a free plan, and what are the limits on it?
source.note: real collected answer; brand, competitors and publishers are the specs the cycle was scored with

answer.text:
Several major CRM providers offer permanent free plans (not just trial periods). The right option depends on whether your main constraint is user count, contact storage, or feature depth.

| CRM | User Limit | Contact/Storage Limit | Key Feature Limits |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **HubSpot CRM** | 2 users | 1,000 contacts | Basic automation (1 action per form); 2,000 marketing email sends/mo; HubSpot branding on forms/emails; 5 shared documents total. |
| **Zoho CRM** | 3 users | 10,000 records total | No workflow automation rules; no custom reporting/dashboards; restricted third-party integrations; standard email templates only. |
| **Freshsales** | 3 users | 1,000 contacts | 1 sales pipeline only; no automated workflows; email support only (no phone support). |
| **Bitrix24** | 5 users | Unlimited contacts (only 1,000 searchable via filter) | 5 GB cloud storage total; basic project management tools; restricted API access for integrations. |
| **Capsule CRM** | 2 users | 250 contacts | 50 MB storage; basic contact tracking and sales pipeline; no email marketing integrations. |
| **EngageBay** | 2 users | 250 contacts | 1,000 branded marketing emails/mo; basic live chat; limited landing pages and autoresponders. |

**General Trade-Offs Across Free Plans**

* **Automation Caps:** Free tiers almost universally lock complex sequence triggers, deal-stage automation, and auto-assignment rules behind paid plans.
* **Branding:** Marketing emails, live chat widgets, and web forms built on free tiers typically display the CRM vendor’s logo.
* **Support:** Direct phone or priority ticketing is generally excluded; free users rely on email support or community forums.
